_description: Fallbacks applied when the env is constructed with a config dict that omits a key - a bare continuousDoubleAuctionEnv({}), a test fixture, or an RLlib env_config that only sets a few keys. Read through config_loader.env_default; the env holds no literal for any of them.
_note: These are STANDALONE defaults and deliberately differ from the training defaults in train_config.json: a bare env is small (num_of_agents 5, max_step 64) and renders, a training env is large and silent. Keys here use the env-side spelling: num_of_agents, not the TrainConfig field name num_agents. TrainConfig.env_config always supplies every key below, so a training run never reaches these.
_note_init_cash: init_cash must be > 0. Trader._order_approved refuses on nav <= 0 before it inspects anything else, so a bare env built with init_cash 0 - as this file shipped until now - starts every trader bankrupt: no order is ever placed, Done_Helper.set_done puts every agent in done_set on the first pass, and terminateds['__all__'] is True after a single step(), so max_step is unreachable. It matches cli_defaults.json and train_config.json at 1,000,000 so all three agree. test_bare_env_is_tradable pins it.

environment._note_mark_price_source: mark_price_source picks the price every account is marked at. 'mid' is the L1 midpoint, falling back to the one-sided quote and then to the last tape print; 'last' is the last tape print alone, which is what this used to do unconditionally. It is a key rather than a constant because the change moves NAV dynamics. Marking off the last print is what made self-matching profitable (finding S2-5): one self-traded contract at a chosen price re-marked the whole market, including the self-trader's own reward - measured at 1,000 NAV moved by a single 1-lot print. Self-match prevention now stops the print from happening, and marking to mid removes the payoff even if some other path ever produces one.
environment._note_position_scale: position_scale divides net_position before the tanh in the private observation block. Deliberately not limit_max_size, which is what it used to be: that is a sizing parameter - it scales the mean of the Gaussian _set_size draws from and bounds nothing - while inventory accumulates over many fills. Measured over 7,200 agent-steps of random play at default config, |net_position| has a median of 372, a p90 of 1,195, a p95 of 1,485 and a maximum of 1,831, so limit_max_size of 1,000 put 13.2% of agent-steps into tanh saturation. 1500 is that p95, which keeps the feature in its responsive range across the observed distribution (finding S2-2).
environment._note_reward_coefficients: Reward coefficients. Every one multiplies a quantity already expressed as a FRACTION OF STARTING NAV (reward_helper.set_reward divides by trader.acc.init_nav), so 1e-05 is one basis point of initial capital. Measured over 8,000 random-agent steps: a step that moves NAV at all moves it by a median 1.9e-03 of starting capital (p90 7.3e-03), and 37% of steps move it at all. The micro-penalties are set at ~0.5-1% of that median move - a nudge on order placement, not a tax that dominates the P&L, which is what finding S2-3 was about when they were 0.1 and 0.05 against raw dollar NAV.
environment._note_drawdown_penalty: drawdown_penalty multiplies the SIGNED CHANGE in drawdown, not the level. The level was charged on all 4,096 steps of an episode, so one early loss taxed every later step even from an idle agent (finding S2-1). Signed rather than clipped at zero: clipping would charge nav_term twice on every losing step and refund nothing on recovery, which is an asymmetric loss multiplier by another name. Signed, the charges telescope to -drawdown_penalty * final_drawdown over an episode, so a round trip is free and the term cannot be farmed.
environment._note_loss_multiplier: loss_multiplier MUST be 1.0 to keep the game zero-sum. Total NAV is conserved exactly, so sum(nav_change) == 0 across agents; any value above 1 makes sum(reward) < 0, which makes passing dominant for every agent and collapses the market (finding S1-3, measured: all-pass scored exactly 0.0 while random trading scored -591,027). It shipped at 1.5.
